Enacted as Title V of Division J of the Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020. It directs a ten-year, whole-of-government strategy to prevent violent conflict and stabilize fragile states, applied first in a small set of priority countries.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 116-94](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/116/public/94){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 9801 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/9801?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 504: a Global Fragility Strategy, issued in 2020 as the U.S. Strategy to Prevent Conflict and Promote Stability.
- Sec. 505: selection of priority countries and regions. In 2022 these were Haiti, Libya, Mozambique, Papua New Guinea, and Coastal West Africa (Benin, Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Togo).
- Sec. 506: ten-year country plans, with biennial reports to Congress.
- Sec. 509: the Prevention and Stabilization Fund and the Complex Crises Fund.
- State leads policy, USAID leads implementation, and Defense supports.

## Why it matters

It is the main statutory expression of conflict prevention as a U.S. foreign policy goal and of long time horizons in assistance planning. It sits with the [Elie Wiesel Act](wiesel-2018.qmd) and the [Women, Peace & Security Act](wps-2017.qmd) as a set of prevention statutes, and it draws on funding authorities in the [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd).

## Current status

The policy framework remains in law, but the funding authorizations ran through fiscal year 2024. Reauthorization bills (H.R. 3005 and S. 2678, 119th Congress) were introduced in 2025 and had not been enacted as of this wiki's last review. Implementation largely stalled in 2025 after USAID and the State Department's conflict and stabilization bureau were dismantled.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 22 U.S.C.](title22-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Sanctions, cyber, and great powers ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 9: Foreign assistance, fragility, and partners](../study/units/assistance.qmd) (core reading).
- **Member lenses.** [Rep. Sara Jacobs](../members/jacobs.qmd): Foreign Affairs; Security Sector Compacts Act.
